title: ‘Final Payment,’ ‘Zoom In, Zoom Out’ Win Big at Pingyao; ‘Congo Boy’ Takes Rossellini Prize
description: Niu Niu’s “Final Payment” and Dong Jie’s “Zoom In, Zoom Out” each won two prizes at the 10th Pingyao Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon International Fil
body:
Niu Niu’s “Final Payment” and Dong Jie’s “Zoom In, Zoom Out” each won two prizes at the 10th Pingyao Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon International Film Festival in China.

	“Final Payment,” from Shanxi-born Niu, won the Fei Mu Award for best film, along with best actor for Niu’s father, Niu Jianrong. “Zoom In, Zoom Out” took the Fei Mu jury award and the Cinephilia Critics’ Award.

	The best film prize carries RMB1 million ($149,000), split equally between the director, for the development of their next film, and the film’s China distributor.
	

	“Tearing through a very small rip, the film leads us into a reality and emotional landscape so expansive, where we sigh, lament, and reflect. The director’s approach is concise, unpretentious, and masterful, earning the wholehearted recognition of the entire jury,” the jury said.


	The film follows a homeowner locked in a standoff with his contractor over the last payment for a renovation, a dispute drawn from Niu Jianrong’s own experience.

	Niu Jianrong, an experienced TV and film director, made his debut as a lead actor in the film. Along with best actress winner Sun Yi, he received a Louis Vuitton accessories box engraved with the festival logo.

	“You jury’s bold for giving me this award,” Niu Jianrong said on stage. “It was such torture, my director-son trained me really hard. In real life, I’m my son’s father; but in front of the camera, he’s my father.”

	Accepting the jury award, Dong said the team approached the film “with absolute purity of intent, which allows me to fully and unreservedly embrace the joy of making it. It’s the joy of conquering something immensely difficult alongside dear friends, the joy of connecting with audiences after the premiere, and, above all, the joy of simply being here, in this very moment.”
	

	Xu Zao won the Unitree best director award for his debut animated feature “Light Pillar,” which carries RMB200,000 ($29,800) toward his next film. The jury cited his “strong aesthetic awareness” and “astute yet warm approach,” which “encourages everyone to hold up the beacon and keep moving forward even on a cold night.”

	Sun won best actress for Wang Xiaozhen’s “A Joke.” The jury said she “delivers a delicate performance with restraint, portraying the regret and growth within an intimate relationship.”

	The Fei Mu jury also gave a special mention to Cai Chengjie’s “Suzhou Quartet,” produced by Huang Bo, “for its bravery, for its belief that the movie screen is still vast and open to new adventures and new forms of storytelling.”

	In the Crouching Tigers international competition, Rafiki Fariala’s “Congo Boy” won the Roberto Rossellini Award for best film and $20,000, split between the director’s next film and the film’s China distributor. The jury cited its “simple style that echoes the great tradition of neorealism.” Fariala, who was not in Pingyao, sent a video thanking the festival and closed it by singing a folk song.

	Rafael Manuel won best director and $10,000 for “Filipiñana,” which Jia Zhangke executive produced and Unknown Pleasures acquired for Greater China.

	Lenti Liang’s “Our Secrets” won the Fei Mu best short film award and RMB50,000 ($7,450), sponsored by Nowness of Meta Media. On stage, Liang said the film drew on her own childhood trauma, and that after her mother saw it in Pingyao, the two talked it through and she had made peace with it.

	Wang Wenting’s “Black Goat” won the Unitree best student short film award in the Pingyao Corner section, with RMB30,000 ($4,470) and a Unitree robot dog.

	Earlier in the festival, Ann Hui received the Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon East-West Award. Pingyao also honored Marco Müller and Han Sanping with the International Contribution to Chinese Cinema Award, and producer Tang Yan, founder of Hello Group, which owns social app Momo, with the 10th Anniversary Award.

	The full list of winners:

	Fei Mu Awards – Hidden DragonsBest Film: “Final Payment,” dir. Niu NiuUnitree Best Director: Xu Zao, “Light Pillar”Best Actress: Sun Yi, “A Joke,” dir. Wang XiaozhenBest Actor: Niu Jianrong, “Final Payment,” dir. Niu NiuJury Award: “Zoom In, Zoom Out,” dir. Dong JieSpecial Mention: “Suzhou Quartet,” dir. Cai ChengjieBest Short Film: “Our Secrets,” dir. Lenti LiangBest Short Film Special Mention: “If a Walnut Falls,” dir. Liu Bohao
	

	Roberto Rossellini Awards – Crouching TigersBest Film: “Congo Boy,” dir. Rafiki FarialaBest Director: Rafael Manuel, “Filipiñana”Jury Award: “Ben’imana,” dir. Marie-Clémentine DusabejamboSpecial Mention: “Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep,” dir. Rakan Mayasi

	Pingyao CornerUnitree Best Student Short Film: “Black Goat,” dir. Wang WentingSpecial Mentions: “Rainforest,” dir. Justine Moo; “Whose Home,” dir. Huang Duojia

	Youth Jury Award: “Whispers in May,” dir. Chen DongnanNetpac Award – Best First Film: “Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep,” dir. Rakan MayasiCinephilia Critics’ Award: “Zoom In, Zoom Out,” dir. Dong JiePYIFF–NAAC Distribution Award: “A Girl Unknown,” dir. Zou Jing

	Honorary AwardsCrouching Tiger Hidden Dragon East-West Award: Ann HuiInternational Contribution to Chinese Cinema Award: Han Sanping, Marco Müller10th Anniversary Award: Tang Yan

title: Christy Carlson Romano Says She and ‘Even Stevens’ Co-Star Shia LaBeouf Were ‘Like Oil and Water’ While Filming the Disney Channel Show
description: Christy Carlson Romano, who first broke out on the Disney Channel sitcom “Even Stevens,” is opening up about her experience working alongside co-sta
body:
Christy Carlson Romano, who first broke out on the Disney Channel sitcom “Even Stevens,” is opening up about her experience working alongside co-star Shia LaBeouf. Speaking with Amanda Hirsch of the Not Skinny But Not Fat podcast on Tuesday, Romano said that she and LaBeouf were “like oil and water,” despite being just 14 and 12 years old, respectively, at the time.

	Romano explained that their incompatibility on set stemmed from how they were raised.
	

	“I was being raised and brought up to be this type A, I mean exactly like Ren Stevens. Like, you know your lines, you hit your marks, you don’t mess up,” she said. “You’re a New York kid, like that comes with a certain echelon… I was trying to go to pre-college Juilliard… everything we were doing, my mom called it cross-training, came with a certain dollar amount of training.”


	In comparison, LaBeouf has long been open about his tumultuous childhood and has said that his father was a recovering addict, and at times abusive. “He was a Venice Beach kind of bum kid,” said Romano. “It’s like that kind of vagrant fun, but also very chaotic and very scary lifestyle, and he was very young to be having that.” She likened his upbringing to the lifestyle depicted in the 1995 Larry Clark film “Kids.”

	Romano did give LaBeouf credit for finding his manager at just eight years old; the “Transformers” and “Holes” star “had a dream and made it happen for himself,” she added.

	“Even Stevens” ran from 2000 to 2003 and followed Ren (Romano) and Louis (LaBeouf), the two younger siblings of the Stevens family who were described as having opposing personalities and often clashing. 
	

	This isn’t the first time Romano has weighed in on her relationship with LaBeouf. Earlier this year, the actress posted — and then deleted — a statement reading “Shia doesn’t deserve to be on the Rushmore. I’ll be writing a Substack on this so you can understand why,” to X. The comment came after “That’s So Raven” star Raven-Symoné was asked who she’d put on her Disney Mount Rushmore, to which she responded that LaBeouf would be one of them.

	On Tuesday, the actress also posted a photo of herself with LaBeouf and his father on the set of “Even Stevens” to Instagram. “Recently found this picture. Shia and I spent 3 years of our lives right next to each other in adjoining trailers, both of us enduring painful childhoods,” she wrote. “If only we could have been there for each other, but we were each going through our own battles and could barely take care of ourselves.” She concluded by writing that she’d “finally” be sharing everything in her forthcoming memoir, “Once Upon a Trainwreck: The Fall and Rise of a Child Star,” which will be available on Oct. 6.

schema.headline: Christy Carlson Romano Says She and ‘Even Stevens’ Co-Star Shia LaBeouf Were ‘Like Oil and Water’ While Filming the Disney Channel Show

title: Lady A’s Charles Kelley Shares Blood Cancer Diagnosis: ‘I’m Confident That We’re Going to Get Through It’
description: Charles Kelley, the co-lead vocalist and founding member of the country band Lady A, has been diagnosed with the rare blood cancer multiple myeloma.
body:
Charles Kelley, the co-lead vocalist and founding member of the country band Lady A, has been diagnosed with the rare blood cancer multiple myeloma. 

	The singer shared the news on his Instagram on Tuesday, with the caption “A little health update” under the video.

	“Hey everybody. Just wanted to give a quick update on some health issues I’m dealing with,” Kelley said. “I had [a] couple random rib fractures that happened, which sparked my doctor into having me do several different blood tests. And one of the last blood tests we did, they found a blood cancer in there called multiple myeloma, and it’s rare.”
	

	“I’m young, I feel healthy, and the treatments I will say have just come so far, even in the past five years,” he continued. “Even life expectancy just far exceeds what it used to be and, I don’t know, I feel really hopeful. I really do.”


	Kelley likened sharing the news of his health with his sobriety journey: “Just getting this stuff off your chest is so freeing, and it takes the power away from it a little bit that we want to let y’all know what was going on. But we’re going to get through it. You know, I think in sobriety it’s all about one day at a time and that we’re not in control, and so that’s the way we’re looking at it.”

	Kelley has been outspoken about his struggles with alcohol, and in 2022, the band — formerly known as Lady Antebellum — shared that they would be postponing the remainder of their “Request Line Tour” in support of Charles Kelley’s “journey to sobriety.”

	The singer concluded the video by sharing that he is “hopeful” and will “try” to let fans in throughout the journey. “It’s just another hurdle, and you know, I’m confident that we’re going to get through it.”
	

	From Dec. 10 through 21, the group will perform a run of Christmas shows as part of the “This Winter’s Night” tour.

schema.headline: Lady A’s Charles Kelley Shares Blood Cancer Diagnosis: ‘I’m Confident That We’re Going to Get Through It’

title: ‘Making Marie Antoinette’: A Mother’s Love Letter to Sofia Coppola’s Genius Charms NYFF
description:
“I enjoyed it, but I’m never doing this again.”

	Sofia Coppola utters those words toward the end of “Making Marie Antoinette,” a feature documentar
body:
“I enjoyed it, but I’m never doing this again.”

	Sofia Coppola utters those words toward the end of “Making Marie Antoinette,” a feature documentary about the making of her 2006 film “Marie Antoinette” from her late mother, Eleanor Coppola.

	Playing in the Spotlight section of the New York Film Festival, the fly-on-the-wall doc is compiled from 80 hours of footage that Eleanor shot during the film’s busy production on location at the Palace of Versailles, capturing a young filmmaker coming into her own before our very eyes (as well as plenty of hijinks from stars Kirsten Dunst and Jason Schwartzman, who plays King Louis XVI and also happens to be Sofia’s cousin). “Marie Antoinette” came out in 2006 to mixed reviews and modest box office returns, but is now regarded as a cult classic.
	

	During the film’s post-premiere Q&A at NYFF, Sofia revealed that the Coppola family were all gathered at their family home in Napa Valley when they decided to revisit Eleanor’s footage for the first time, and it brought back a rush of memories from her time making “Marie Antoinette.” “It’s embarrassing for me,” Sofia said after the film. “When I’m in the trailer complaining that I don’t want to talk to my mom and being not nice… but it’s important to show all the sides, and I’m crabby sometimes!”




	Though Eleanor passed away in 2024 at the age of 87, she was “always frustrated that the footage was never put together [into a film],” so Sofia — with the help of editor Aaron Matthews — helped make her vision a reality. Eleanor envisioned an observational film in the vein of Frederick Wiseman, and the doc is narrated by actress Diane Lane, a longtime Coppola family collaborator, who reads Eleanor’s contemporaneous diary entries from twenty years ago. “There wasn’t much drama, so how do you make it not boring?” Sofia pondered during the Q&A.
	

	Although there was some drama. We see Sofia and her team on “Marie Antoinette” overwhelmed at times by the amount of extras and just how long it took cast members to get their hair, makeup and costuming done (the hair, especially). In addition to a monument to Sofia, “Making Marie Antoinette” is also a celebration of the work of Milena Canonero, the film’s costume designer. Canonero created over 70 original dresses for Dunst’s Marie Antoinette alone, and eventually won the Academy Award for Best Costume Design.

	The most compelling scenes in “Making Marie Antoinette,” scheduled to be released Oct. 23 on Mubi, concern Sofia butting heads with her cinematographer, Lance Acord, who wanted more shots showing the perspective of King Louis XVI instead of centering the POV of Marie Antoinette. It’s stirring to see Sofia, who was 34 at the time, push back on Acord’s demands and stay true to her vision. “It’s hard to believe twenty years ago that the female point-of-view was so unusual,” she said during the Q&A. “Now I’m more comfortable at being assertive at what I want… I was still trying to find my way of being assertive on set about what I wanted.”

	We also get to take in Schwartzman fooling around on set, playing the harpsichord and cracking jokes to a tiny dog; Dunst giving it her all with a smile; and Asia Argento, who played the icy Madame du Berry, throwing her shoulder into Dunst way too hard during a confrontation scene. Oh, and we also see Thomas Mars, the lead singer of Phoenix and Coppola’s then-boyfriend, be introduced to Eleanor for the first time (Sofia and Thomas are now married with two children).

	But mostly we bear witness to Sofia executing her vision with precision and grace. It’s a sight to behold, as is this love letter from mother to daughter (and vice versa). “I get stressed watching it and just seeing how none of us were prepared for a period film and how long the costume changes would take,” Sofia confessed during the Q&A, but added, “I felt so lucky that [my mother] gave this to me, and to have this tribute to her and being with her again.”

schema.headline: ‘Making Marie Antoinette’: A Mother’s Love Letter to Sofia Coppola’s Genius Charms NYFF

title: Casey Bloys Poised to Run HBO and Paramount+ as Cindy Holland Confirms Her Exit From Studio on Eve of Merger Closing
description: HBO chief Casey Bloys is poised to take the reins of all of Paramount and Warner Bros. streaming operations once the two companies merge. On Tuesday
body:
HBO chief Casey Bloys is poised to take the reins of all of Paramount and Warner Bros. streaming operations once the two companies merge. On Tuesday, Cindy Holland announced she was stepping down from her role running Paramount+ and other direct to consumer streamers under the Paramount umbrella.

	The shuffle comes as Paramount Skydance is days away from closing its hard-won $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.


	Holland confirmed her departure in a memo to staff sent Tuesday afternoon, acknowledging that Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison has made the decision regarding streaming leadership, although she did not reference Bloys by name.
	

	“As David readies for the next phase of his vision, we’ve discussed my role and the future of the combined businesses. David is optimizing for HBO stability as we move into this next chapter, and I fully support that. I know this team has the leadership and expertise to manage through the transition and the next phase of the company, and to this end today will mark my last day here,” Holland wrote.

	Over the past few weeks, speculation emerged that Bloys was likely to come over post merger in the top role overseeing all streaming operations. Bloys is a near 25-year veteran of HBO who has steered TV’s most prestigious brand through choppy waters and three massive corporate takeovers in eight years. There’s also speculation that JB Perrette, who now heads streaming business operations and gaming for WBD, will join Bloys in steering HBO, HBO Max and Paramount+. 

	Holland was part of the pioneering team that built Netflix into the world’s biggest subscription streaming platform. Her 18-year run at that streamer included nine years as Vice President of Original Content. Holland established the network’s original programming strategy and oversaw the teams behind flagship hits like “House of Cards,” “Stranger Things,” “The Crown,” “Icarus,” “When They See Us” and “The Queen’s Gambit.” Between Netflix and Paramount, Holland served as CEO of Sister — the production company formed by Elizabeth Murdoch. Her exit comes as the industry speculates wildly about the fate of other division leaders across both companies.
	

	Here is Holland’s full memo:

	When I joined David’s team in January 2025, we proceeded to set three goals: i) advise on the Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition, ii) integrate and transform Paramount+ & revive Pluto TV, and iii) build an unparalleled team in this industry. In just over 12 months, I’m proud to say we accomplished all three and it’s been a joy to work closely with all of you.

	Together with the Product team, we drove significant strategic and organizational change across DTC — building a new foundation for growth on both services, while investing in greater depth and breadth of programming and delivering strong revenue, profit, and subscriber growth for the division.

	As David readies for the next phase of his vision, we’ve discussed my role and the future of the combined businesses. David is optimizing for HBO stability as we move into this next chapter, and I fully support that. I know this team has the leadership and expertise to manage through the transition and the next phase of the company, and to this end today will mark my last day here.

	As I reflect on my time here and all that we’ve built together in this short time, what stands out most to me is this team. I have never been more proud of a group of people. What we’ve accomplished together is remarkable — landing quarter after quarter while navigating extraordinary uncertainty and change with resilience, focus and ambition. We grew Paramount+ to an all-time subscriber high, delivered the best retention in the service’s history, and drove double-digit growth in both engagement and revenue. We built an extraordinary content pipeline, greenlighting more than 40 new and returning series and setting all-time records with Landman, the most-watched series in Paramount+ history, and Dutton Ranch, the service’s biggest original series debut ever. We transformed live sports into a powerful streaming growth engine, securing landmark agreements with UFC and Zuffa Boxing and expanding our WNBA and UEFA Champions League rights – with UFC Freedom 250 becoming the largest-ever audience for an exclusive live event on Paramount+ and UFC 329 setting a new platform record for peak concurrent streams for an exclusive live event. And we undertook Pluto TV’s biggest product transformation in a decade, dramatically increasing registered viewing and VOD consumption while delivering strong financial performance across the business. These are extraordinary accomplishments – but what makes me proudest is how we achieved them: together, with an unwavering commitment to our audiences, our creative partners and one another.
	

	I joined Paramount because I believe in these businesses, and because I believe wholeheartedly that the combination of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery serves the best interests of artists and audiences worldwide. I’m looking forward to seeing what you all accomplish together in this next, momentous chapter.

schema.headline: Casey Bloys Poised to Run HBO and Paramount+ as Cindy Holland Confirms Her Exit From Studio on Eve of Merger Closing

body:

title: Penn Badgley Swore Off Sex Scenes. His Wife Says It Was Not Her Idea: ‘He Decided to Do This for Mental Health Reasons’
description: Penn Badgley infamously swore off sex scenes before the production of “You” Season 4, revealing on a viral episode of his “Podcrushed” podcast in Fe
body:
Penn Badgley infamously swore off sex scenes before the production of “You” Season 4, revealing on a viral episode of his “Podcrushed” podcast in Feb. 2013 that he told showrunner Sera Gamble he was no longer interested in filming intimate scenes on camera. The actor then told Variety later that same month that “it’s important to me in my real life to not have” sex scenes, clarifying: “My fidelity in my relationship. It’s important to me.”
	

	Cut to more than three years later and Badgley’s wife, Domino Kirke-Badgley, is speaking out after spending all this time being accused online of blocking her husband from doing sex scenes. When Badgley cited his marriage as a reason he did not want to act in sex scenes anymore, social media was quick to come for Kirke-Badgley, even though Penn had cited her as the reason he even accepted the lusty lead role in “You” in the first place.


	“A few years ago, the internet decided I’d asked my husband to stop doing sex scenes. The truth is, my husband decided to do this for mental health reasons,” Kirke-Badgley wrote on Instagram. “After working in the industry since he was just 12 years old, believe me, it was time. In the entertainment world, they call actors ‘puppets’ behind their backs, and it’s even more disturbing when they start out as child actors… after years of trying, Penn decided to take a stand and let the world see him. And guess what, he hasn’t lost fans and he’s still getting hired!”

	“The characters that my husband has played over the years, people have come to expect that he will continue to play that guy,” she added in the video post. “I was super happy for him and very proud of him because I understood how major it was, and yeah … it’s just relational hygiene.”
	

	Badgley has been married since 2017 to Kirke-Badgley, who “encouraged” him to play Joe on “You” even though the part required him to film various sex scenes.

	“There’s almost nothing I could say with more consecration. That aspect of Hollywood has always been very disturbing to me — and that aspect of the job, that mercurial boundary — has always been something that I actually don’t want to play with at all,” Badgely told Variety in 2023. “I told [Sara Gamble before Season 4] kind of my desire, and she immediately was accepting and responsive. I’m always very practical. I said I know it can’t be none, because there’s something coded into the DNA of the show, and I signed the contract, and so it is what it is but as little as possible would be my preference.”

	There were fewer sex scenes in “You” Season 4, and all of them were performed fully clothed as a result of Badgley speaking up. The actor’s initial comments earned a polarizing response online, with his detractors criticizing him for equating sex scenes with real sex. Many of Badgley’s critics pointed out that intimacy coordinators are now a staple in Hollywood so that sex scenes remain safe during filming. He later told GQ magazine that his comments got “blown out of proportion.”

	“What I was speaking about wasn’t actually the final product,” Badgley said. “It was sort of like the culture inherent to the production of all movies, but particularly those scenes. It’s like, look, we know that Hollywood has had a history of flagrant exploitation and abuse.”

	Badgley said he was “nervous to even have that conversation” with “You” showrunner Sera Gamble, adding, “It was not easy. It was easy because of Sera’s response, and I felt relieved. But technically speaking, if I thought I’d had the ability to set that boundary earlier, I would have. We shall see if setting that boundary, of course, has any ramifications. Just simply, it does limit the number of projects you can be a part of.”

	Next up for Badgley is the romantic comedy “You Deserve Each Other,” co-starring Meghann Fahy.

title: Tom Cruise Pulls Out ‘Risky Business’ Dance Moves for ‘Jennifer Hudson Show’ Spirit Tunnel
description: Tom Cruise pulled out his “Risky Business” dance moves (and those black Ray-Ban sunglasses) for his much-anticipated walk down “The Jennifer Hudson
body:
Tom Cruise pulled out his “Risky Business” dance moves (and those black Ray-Ban sunglasses) for his much-anticipated walk down “The Jennifer Hudson Show’s” Spirit Tunnel.

	The talk show appearance is Cruise’s latest stop on the press tour for “Digger,” directed by two-time Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro González Iñárritu. In her Variety Power of Women cover story, Hudson revealed she booked the movie star as a guest during a chance meeting this summer at the World Cup final.
	

	“I was like, ‘Tom, could you imagine your Spirit Tunnel? What do you think they’re going to sing for you?’” Hudson said, shooting her shot. 


	For the uninitiated: the “Jennifer Hudson Show’s” spirit tunnel is a pre-show segment where her staff lines a hallway at Warner Bros.’ Studio 1 and sings a customized song to welcome each celebrity guest to the stage. Fortunately for Hudson, Cruise knew what he’d be signing up for — “I watch the show, Jennifer,” he told her. “I watch everything. I watched you on ‘American Idol.’” — and, as a new clip shows, he came ready to boogie.

	The video, posted to social media on Tuesday, shows Cruise exiting the dressing room to find “The Jennifer Hudson Show” staff rocking black sunglasses and singing a riff on the classic, “Old Time Rock & Roll.”

	The song calls back to one of Cruise’s first movie star-making moments from the 1983 movie “Risky Business,” where he slides into frame to lip-sync and dance in his underwear and shades to Bob Seger’s version of the song.

	Here, the talk show producers remix the lyrics to reference Cruise’s status as a cinema legend: “We’ve got Tom Cruise at the Happy Place. He’s in the tunnel walking to the stage,” the crew sings. “He’s a legend everybody knows. We’ve got that Tom Cruise rock and roll.”
	

	Cruise quickly commits to the bit, pulling out his own black sunglasses and dancing along, even pulling in some staffers to join him. (Sure, some of his hand claps are off-beat, but Cruise is just as gleefully game here as he is to doing his own stunts in the “Mission: Impossible” movies.)

	Likewise, “Digger,” in theaters Friday, is a massive test of Cruise’s dedication. In the film, he plays Digger Rockwell, a Texas oil tycoon whose company may have set off an ecological disaster that could also spark a nuclear war. The role required Cruise to transform with prosthetics (including a fat suit and thinning white hair) and a put-on Southern accent, but, mostly, the absurdist satire demanded his full acting range. The result is a theatrical showcase seemingly crafted to put Cruise back in the competitive Oscar race for the first time in decades.

	“I have never had something that could challenge me in this way, and neither has Alejandro,” Cruise said about starring in the black comedy.

	The Warner Bros. movie is a big swing, and reviews have been wide-ranging (including Variety’s), so the studio has gone on offense, confronting the negative buzz with a new ad that includes both positive and negative reactions, inviting moviegoers to “decide for yourself.”

	Viewers have to wait until Wednesday to see Cruise’s full interview, but watch his full Spirit Tunnel performance in the clip below:

title: ‘What Remains’ Review: A Pensive but Stirring Drama Finds Poetry in the Landscapes of Rural Turkey
description: If you love something, let it go, the adage advises, and maybe it will come back to you. Maybe, however, it will go and go and go and never come bac
body:
If you love something, let it go, the adage advises, and maybe it will come back to you. Maybe, however, it will go and go and go and never come back, and that, so Yeşim Ustaoğlu’s increasingly lyrical and persuasive “What Remains” would have it, might be its own sort of reclamation. The slowly built, gently revolutionary assertion of this delicate film is that there are some relationships that are stronger and deeper after separation; some lovers who love best with a lot of air and wind between them and you. Perhaps the more space opens up around them, the more affection they generate to fill it.
	

	And perhaps that’s because there are some — you could call them introverts, you could call them solipsists, or you could cut straight to the point and call them writers — who have an essentially solitary streak, no matter how profound and various their attachments to others. Elif (Ökyü Karayel) is one such, a poet of some renown in her native Turkey who has not written a lot recently, or rather, what she has written does not seem to scratch the poet’s itch; whatever creative wellspring she relies on is running dry, its waters coming up sludgy and brackish. 


	Instead she spends her days feeding the curiosity of her bright, precocious son Selim (Ali Kayra Kul), going on long walks through hilly urban Istanbul, watching over a jar of cocooning butterflies and helping him build Rube Goldberg devices in the living room of their pleasantly bohemian apartment. One room of it has recently been converted into a studio of sorts for her partner Mehmet (Metin Akdülger), an experimental musician who is as likely to want to record the sound of a malfunctioning kitchen appliance as to fix it.
	

	It all builds up a picture of quite a privileged, if hardly lucrative, creative-class lifestyle, and in the early going there is a slight sense that maybe too much of our attention is being lavished on this attractive family unit and their rather wan predicaments. But then Mehmet is let go from his job teaching esoteric music practices to university students and the household’s sole steady source of income is gone. It precipitates an argument between the couple — the whispered-so-as-not-to-wake-the-kid kind — in which Elif’s unhappiness comes out haltingly, inarticulately, and all of Mehmet’s suppressed resentments too, as we finally get some idea of just how dysfunctional they have become. Elif has not showered in weeks and barely eats. Mehmet tries to proffer practical solutions but each one only seems to deepen the rift. “I really didn’t understand the extent of your problem,” he says coolly at one point and Elif recoils as if hit.

	Later there is a kind of ceasefire and they make love in the shower into which Mehmet has bodily dragged her. But it is not a reconciliation, it is a farewell — as the next day before daybreak, Elif gets in the car and starts to drive, out of the city into the changing countryside of Turkey, through tunnels and along highways, amid vast empty landscapes and past ancient cities that rise from the plains like the citadels of a fantasy epic. At some point on her hitherto aimless road trip, she realizes where it is she wants to go: to the tiny village in the mountains where her grandmother lived out her days.

	This is not an abandonment. An unusual feature of Ustaoğlu’s thoughtful screenplay is that while this type of narrative, especially when it pertains to a woman and doubly so if she’s a mother, is usually full of recrimination, Elif’s escape is not something for which she is forced to sacrifice all else. In particular, she maintains regular contact with her beloved Selim, Facetime-ing him from the road, and stays in touch with Mehmet, who, with seemingly little complaint, has taken over as the day-to-day parent. And when Mehmet’s aging father becomes ill and he takes Selim along with him to look after him, Mehmet himself also goes on a journey of self-discovery as a son, as a father and as the son of a father he loves, but does not wish to emulate.
	

	Gradually, in fact, the harsh judgments we may have laid on Elif loosen their hold and fall away, especially in seeing her interact with three women she meets at different intervals along the way, who are all solitary but not lonely, all in their way, self-sufficient and resourceful. Their kindness and concern for her, their hospitality so lightly given, starts to reflect back on Elif. She visibly relaxes, her face — and Karayel has a beautiful, lucid face on which we read changes of mood the way we read patterns in clouds — loses its tension. It’s all so well and subtly done that we can be tricked into not seeing that this too is some clever scripting: We start to like Elif at almost exactly the same time she starts to like herself.

	Against the stunning landscapes of wild, remote Turkey, captured in glorious detail by cinematographer Kiril Prodanov, Elif finds her muse again. In the poem she writes near the end of the film (all Elif’s writings are supplied by celebrated Turkish poet Birhan Keskin), she refers to Mehmet as “my crooked tooth, my friend” with moving gratitude, for all that they have been to each other, but partly, we infer, also for letting all of it go. “What Remains” is a beautifully calm manifesto for the idea that self-acceptance is the primary love without which none of the other loves — of partner, of child, of art, of thy neighbor — is truly possible. But in this unusually even-handed relationship drama, it cuts both ways and both Elif and Mehmet emerge the stronger for it. When you love something, and you let it go, you are also releasing yourself from its grip.

schema.headline: ‘What Remains’ Review: A Pensive but Stirring Drama Finds Poetry in the Landscapes of Rural Turkey

title: Presley Gerber Video at Sober House, What Really Happened
description:
Presley Gerber
                          High in Sober House On Video the Night He Died ...
body:
Presley Gerber
                          High in Sober House On Video the Night He Died ...
                          What Really Happened
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                September 29, 2026
                
                            3:24 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 29, 2026
                                7:59 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            TMZ has obtained a video of Presley Gerber at the sober house where he died, and sources with direct knowledge have filled in the blanks for us ... and the circumstances of his death are shocking.
      
    
            The video was shot by Presley inside the Santa Monica facility, Resolutions Living, around 10 PM Saturday night. He appears in a bedroom and other areas of the house. There is no one else in sight.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            It is apparent Presley is high. The video is jumpy because we slowed it down.
      

            Presley is giving a tour of the sober house, showing the bedroom and other areas.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Sources with direct knowledge tell TMZ, Presley got high Saturday afternoon and became scared he was losing control. Sources with direct knowledge tell us, his sober coach called Resolutions Living and asked if he could bring Presley in to the sober house, but confessed that Presley was high on drugs. Our sources say the admissions officer said they would be glad to take him.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Owners of multiple rehab facilities tell TMZ ... it is cardinal rule in rehab not to send someone who is high to a sober house.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Our sources say the sober coach had planned to take Presley to a rehab facility the following Monday but need to put him somewhere over the weekend, so he took him to Resolutions and just left him there.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            We're also told Presley was using drugs inside the facility, which he presumably thought was his last weekend to indulge before entered rehab. He never made it there ... he was found dead Sunday morning.
      
    
            Sources connected to Resolutions tell TMZ the admissions officer was fired. We have made multiple calls to the sober coach, the admissions officer and the owner of Resolutions ... so far, no word back.

            "Alaskan Bush People" star Gabriel Brown's wife, Raquell Brown, has filed for divorce after seven years of marriage.
      
    
            Raquell filed the paperwork September 22, claiming their marriage is "irretrievably broken," according to court docs obtained by Us Weekly.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            TMZ broke the story in July the couple had separated after seven years of marriage.
      

            According to court docs, Raquell and Gabe have been living in separate homes since April. Raquell currently resides in Minnesota, while Gabe lives in Washington. They share three children.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Raquell says the couple has no real property, but she's asking the court to fairly divide their personal belongings and assign each of them responsibility for debts incurred after their separation.
      
    
            She's also reserving the right to seek temporary and permanent spousal support, and wants Gabe to cover her attorney fees and other divorce related costs.
      
    
            In addition, Raquell is seeking child support, medical support and contributions toward their children’s daycare, long-distance transportation and education expenses including future college or vocational school costs.
      
    
            Raquell is also asking the court to approve her proposed parenting plan.

title: Farrah Abraham's Scary Stitching Revealed After Major Jaw Surgery
description:
Farrah Abraham
                          My Jaw's Wired Shut
                          I Feel Lik
body:
Farrah Abraham
                          My Jaw's Wired Shut
                          I Feel Like Frankenstein!!!
                      
      
    
            Farrah Abraham won't be chatting with fans online for at least a little while ... because she's undergone major jaw surgery -- and her mouth is wired shut.
      
    
            Check out the new photos of the former "Teen Mom" star laid up in a hospital bed Friday ... recovering after she clearly went through a facial procedure.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Her cheeks and jaw look swollen after the surgery ... and she's not smiling in any of the pics. Unclear if she can smile even if she wants to.
      

            Several of the photos specifically focus on extensive stitches which run up and down the sides of her face near her ears and across her neck.
      
    
            We spoke with Farrah ... who tells us she got double disc jaw surgery and had custom jaws -- engineered for her face -- implanted.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Farrah says she had to go through the surgery because of an injury she suffered during a reported alleged sexual assault. She claims Dominic Foppoli -- a man she is suing for an alleged sexual assault -- caused the injury to her. She did not get into details about how he allegedly did so.
      
    
            Dominic has vehemently denied any wrongdoing in the lawsuit ... and is not facing criminal charges in connection with Farrah's allegations.
      
    
            Dominic's lawyer tells TMZ, "Mr. Foppoli denies wrongdoing and indicates the encounter with Farrah was consensual.  It is more likely that Farrah is taking the opportunity to have elective surgery and is blaming it on my client in order to make him pay for it."
      
    
            Farrah says she has screws in her gums and her jaw is wired shut. She says her nerves are mending back together ... and she hopes she can regain some hearing in her right ear soon. She claims she had jaw and skull scans done after the incident as well as physical therapy, but this procedure was her only option to fix the synthetic nerve damage.
      
    
            Despite the difficult procedure, Farrah is looking much better after the weekend ... on Monday, she appeared in her daughter Sophia's TikTok Live, and the stitches weren't visible.
      
    
            She posted on her Instagram story about her current state ... writing she feels like Frankenstein at the moment -- and praying her face rebounds in a few months.

            Her point ... under New York law, voluntary intoxication alone does not automatically erase someone's ability to consent. Sunny said she believes women, but argued the 2024 statement and the allegations in a new lawsuit filed last week are different.
